title: `Core\Xml` is a materialising tree beside a one-window stream, and it refuses a document type declaration whole
scope:
the two shapes `Core\Xml` offers and why they share no operation; what a strict XML parse
refuses and why each refusal is an absent code path rather than a bounded one; where a `<!DOCTYPE …>`
stops. Not in scope: the node family and the WHATWG parser that shares it, which are
[0122](0122.md)'s and are not reopened here; the members' signatures, which
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/xml.rs` declares; the compression bound this record declines to reuse, which is
[0154](0154.md)'s.
dependsOnText:
[0122](0122.md) — the node family both doors produce, and
the refuse-hard contract this record gives its refusals to; [0051](0051.md)
— `Core\Xml` as Tier 0, one API replacing six extensions;
[0019](0019.md) — inert parsed data with no path back into execution.

summary.headline: XML is a whole tree or a one-window stream, and a DOCTYPE is refused outright
summary.body:
`Core\Xml` offers a tree that loads the whole document and answers walks in any order, and a
reader and writer that hold one element at a time. No operation is available through both, so a
program picks the shape for how much of the document it needs at once and pays for that alone.
There is no code that resolves an entity, so external entities are not a setting that could be
left on, and a `<!DOCTYPE>` is refused whole, which ends the billion-laughs family before it
starts. Nesting depth is the one numeric bound.
